**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The assignment clause at paragraph (h) satisfies the preferred position on its material terms:

- **AP's assignment freedom** — AP may assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all assets related to the subject matter, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation. The M&A carve-out we require is present.
- **Consent standard** — any other assignment requires prior written consent "which shall not be unreasonably withheld," matching the playbook standard.
- **No change-of-control exposure** — no "change of control" or "deemed an assignment" language appears anywhere in the document. Termination (paragraph 4) is limited to post-Initial-Term 90-day notice, uncured material breach, and insolvency, so Kubient has no right to terminate or re-price if AP is acquired. Walk-away territory is not implicated.

Two sub-elements sit short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted in the rationale rather than redlined:

1. The free-assignment carve-out is **mutual**, so Kubient may likewise assign to its own affiliate or acquirer without our consent — this is precisely the playbook fallback (mutual right to assign to successors with consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld), which is acceptable and not redlined.
2. There is no express prohibition on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor.

Given the clause already delivers our M&A carve-out and carries no change-of-control trigger, neither gap is material enough to justify opening the provision.
